rules.rule: Check for causes of crusts or flaky skin
rules.problem: Type and trigger match 'Are there crusts or flaky skin?'. Every discriminating finding of the four 'likely' branches is listed and consumed. The red box on this page only points to page 82, so the absence of a priority evaluation is correct. Minor: 'May have pitted nails' (Pitting of nails, disorder exists) and the seborrhoeic/psoriasis site lists ('Usually'/'Often') are not encoded; acceptable since the page hedges them.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable impetigo (crusts or flaky skin)
rules.problem: Requires Blister of skin AND yellow crusts. The page's Crusts branch reads 'Blisters which dry to form yellow crusts' and then 'Impetigo likely': blisters are the precursor lesion, and a patient presenting with yellow crusts only (the blisters having already dried) matches the page but not the rule. Probable level is right ('likely').

rules.rule: Diagnose probable seborrhoeic dermatitis (crusts or flaky skin)
rules.problem: AND of scaly + erythema + greasy follows 'Red/pink scaly patches with fine, greasy scales'. Greasy skin is a proxy for 'greasy scales' and Erythema of skin would be a closer concept than Erythema; neither changes the page's logic. Probable level is right.

rules.rule: Diagnose probable psoriasis (crusts or flaky skin)
Diagnose probable eczema (crusts or flaky skin)
rules.problem: (and (or four flexural/wrist/ankle sites) Xeroderma Itching) matches 'Patches of dry, scaly, itchy skin on wrists, ankles, inside elbows or behind knees'. The site is attached to Scaly skin only, with dryness and itch recorded sitelessly; a reasonable approximation. Probable level is right.

summary: Nothing on this page is invented and all four 'likely' diagnoses are correctly at probable; the only logic problem is the impetigo rule, which requires blisters to be present together with yellow crusts although the page presents blisters as the precursor that dries into the crusts, so crusts-only presentations are missed. Secondary: 'greasy scales' is encoded as Greasy skin (no closer concept exists) and bare Erythema could be Erythema of skin. No priority evaluation is needed because the red box only refers to page 82.
